chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Uthman, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi al-Mughira, from Abu Umara al-Munshid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

He (peace be upon him) said to me, 'O Abu Umara, recite for me the poem of al-Abdi regarding al-Husayn (peace be upon him).' I said, 'So I recited it to him and he wept.' He said, 'Then I recited it to him and he wept.' He said, 'By God, I continued reciting it to him while he wept until I heard the weeping from the house.'

Then he (peace be upon him) said to me, 'O Abu Umara! One who recites a poem regarding al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) and makes fifty people cry, for him is Paradise. And one who recites regarding al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and makes forty people cry, for him is Paradise. And one who recites regarding al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and makes thirty people cry, for him is Paradise. And one who recites regarding al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and makes twenty people cry, for him is Paradise. And one who recites regarding al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and makes ten people cry, for him is Paradise.'

And one who recites regarding al-Husayn a single poem, for him is Paradise. And one who recites regarding al-Husayn (peace be upon him) a poem and cries, for him is Paradise. And one who recites regarding al-Husayn (peace be upon him) a poem and makes a crying face, for him is Paradise.

key_terms.تَبَاکَی: Made a crying face / showed signs of weeping

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting poetry about Imam Husain and making people cry?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A’mal* highlights the profound spiritual merit of *sha’r al-Husayniyya* (poetry about Imam Husayn) as a means of preserving his legacy and evoking *mawadda* (affection) in the hearts of the faithful. The graded rewards emphasize that even minimal engagement with Husayn’s narrative—whether through a single verse or a subtle change in expression—carries the promise of Paradise, underscoring the accessibility of this devotional act in Shia tradition.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s.) told Abu Umara, “Recite a poem regarding  Imam  Husain  (a.s.).”  He  recited  the  poem  and Imam (a.s.) cried. He went on reciting and Imam (a.s.) cried continuously till the wails started coming out of his house.

Then Imam (a.s.) said, “O Abu Umara! One who recites a poem regarding Imam Husain (a.s.) and makes fifty persons cry Paradise belongs to him. One who recites a poem and forty persons cry Paradise is for them. If thirty persons cry Paradise  is  for  them  also.  One  who  recites  a  poem  and twenty  persons  cry  they  too  will  get  Paradise.  One  who makes ten people cry after reciting a poem of Imam Husain (a.s.) they too will get Paradise.

One who makes a person cry after reciting a poem of Imam Husain (a.s.) they too will get Paradise. One  who  recites  the  poem  of  Imam  Husain (a.s.)  and  cries  alone  he  too  will  get  Paradise.  One  who makes just a crying face after reciting the poem regarding Imam Husain (a.s.) he too will get Paradise.”
